newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: Creditors to supply 8.0 bln won to Jinro.
newsitem.headline: Creditors to supply 8.0 bln won to Jinro.

text.p: Creditor banks have decided to supply eight billion won to troubled Jinro General Foods Co and extend its principal payments for one year, its major creditor Hanil Bank said on Wednesday.
They said they would not extend bail-out benefits for the company. Those benefits expire on Sunday.

Jinro General Foods had not been given any emergency funds so far because Jinro group chairman Chang Jin-ho had not submitted a letter giving up management rights in the company, a bank official said.
Jinro's creditors are due to meet on Friday to discuss the future of the group.
In April, the 19th-ranked Jinro Group buckled under 3.2 trillion won in debt, mostly a result of reckless expansion.
Shares of Jinro General Foods closed at a new yearly low of 3,390 won on Wednesday, down 290.
On Tuesday, Jinro creditor banks said they would not extend bail-out benefits for any group affiliates.
